title: CPG Food Trends for 2027
summary: Our work gives us a front-row seat to where the better-for-you industry is heading. Here are the food trends we expect to see on store shelves in 2027.
body_markdown:
[Manufacturing](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog-categories/manufacturing/) ,


[Trends](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog-categories/trends/)


November 11, 2026


From the show floor of[Natural Products Expo West](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog/trends-expo-west-2026/) to within the four walls of our own production facility, we talk to founders innovating in the CPG space every day. Those conversations give us a front-row seat to where the better-for-you industry is heading. Expect to see more of the following food trends on store shelves in 2027.


## Natural Colors


Brands have until the end of 2027 to meet the deadline for the FDA’s voluntary phase-out of six petroleum-based dyes (Red 40, Yellow 5, Yellow 6, Blue 1, Blue 2, and Green 3). While the phase-out is voluntary, consumer demand is pushing many brands to introduce natural lines or reformulate products.


A[recent report](https://candyusa.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Natural-Colorant-Roadmap_Digital.pdf) by The National Confectioners Association (NCA) and RTI International shows sales of products with “natural colors” listed as an ingredient grew 24.4% across food and beverage categories in 2025. Items labeled with artificial colors only increased 0.1%.


PepsiCo introduced a[Simply NKD](https://www.pepsico.com/newsroom/stories/2025/cheetos-and-doritos-are-getting-naked) line of colorless Cheetos and Doritos at the end of 2025, which accrued more than $3 million in sales in its first month of availability. Introducing alternative products alongside legacy SKUs allows brands to test consumer acceptance of dye-free versions.


Retail commitments may also further this trend. For example,[Target stopped carrying cereals made with synthetic dyes](https://www.fastcompany.com/91500214/target-synthetic-dyes-cereal) . Walmart plans to[remove synthetic dyes](https://www.fastcompany.com/91414193/walmart-is-quietly-changing-your-groceries-heres-whats-disappearing) from its private label products by January 2027.


Natural colorants can behave differently than synthetic dyes, so getting the color, taste, and shelf life right often takes some testing and adjustment. The Fresh Factory has been dye-free from the start, and we’re seeing more brands come to us for help reformulating.


## Hydroponics


During the 2026 cyclospora outbreak, hydroponic brands like Gotham Greens won consumer trust by being transparent about how their products were grown. As a result, Gotham Greens notes its website traffic from July 9 to 19[jumped more than 800%](https://www.modernretail.co/marketing/we-arent-impacted-lettuce-brands-are-on-an-awareness-push-amid-the-cyclospora-outbreak/) over the previous 10 days. That interest carried over to the register, with the company reporting[18% year-over-year retail sales growth](https://www.thepacker.com/news/riding-indoor-grown-demand-surge-gotham-greens-charts-its-next-phase-growth) across its packaged salads, herbs, salad kits, dressings, dips, and cooking sauces.


Leafy greens are just the start. Indoor strawberry grower Oishii[closed the first round of a $150 million Series C in May 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oishii-announces-first-closing-of-150m-in-series-c-financing-as-it-scales-its-indoor-smart-farm-model-302770199.html) . Plenty opened an[indoor strawberry farm](https://www.plenty.ag/plenty-opens-worlds-first-farm-to-grow-indoor-vertically-farmed-berries-at-scale/) in Richmond, Virginia, built to produce more than 4 million pounds a year. Greenhouse tomatoes have also gone mainstream, with greenhouse-grown varieties, including hydroponic, making up[40% to 50% of retail tomato sales](https://producebusiness.com/selling-tomatoes-what-works/) in many regions.


This shift lines up with what major retailers expect consumers to look for next year. In its[2027 trends report](https://press.aboutamazon.com/2026/10/whole-foods-market-reveals-its-top-food-and-beverage-trend-predictions-for-2027) , Whole Foods Market named terroir, or a desire for a “taste of place” and product origin, as a top trend. Shoppers want to know where their food comes from, and hydroponic brands can answer that question with confidence.


## Functional Foods


We talked about[functional food trends](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog/functional-foods-2026/) at the start of 2026, and we expect consumers to keep reaching for products that do more than satisfy hunger in 2027. Foods for skin health, coined “beautrition” in Whole Foods’ trend predictions, is an area particularly on the rise. To support healthy skin, consumers look for ingredient lists rich in collagen, antioxidants, and healthy fats.


[Innova food trends](https://www.innovamarketinsights.com/trends/top-10-food-trends-2027/) show increased interest in functional foods, too. Their recent report notes:


- 35% of consumers want ingredients that support healthy aging, like creatine
- 38% of consumers reach for fermented foods that support gut health
- 39% of consumers want food and beverage products that help maintain steady energy


## Fiber-Forward


Fiber was one of the main trends we saw at Natural Products Expo West earlier this year, with products and messaging focused on digestive health and satiety.[The Vitamin Shoppe’s Health & Wellness Trend Report for 2026](https://press.vitaminshoppe.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/The-Vitamin-Shoppe-Health-Wellness-Trend-Report-2026.pdf) notes its fiber category was up 20% in sales for the year, led by double-digit growth in fiber combination products. In addition, fiber search terms on The Vitamin Shoppe website showed year-over-year increases:


- Fiber: 59% growth
- Fiber gummies: 90% growth
- Psyllium husk: 150% growth


We expect fiber to remain on the main stage in 2027, too. This is largely playing out in a “bean boom,” according to Whole Foods. As an affordable source of protein and fiber, legumes are becoming a popular food item. While the “dense bean salad” is taking over TikTok feeds, bean formats are also becoming prominent in the snack aisle. Expect to see more edamame and chickpea snacks in the near future.


## A Bitter Taste


Sweet and heat have had their moment, and consumers are expanding their palate to incorporate more bitter notes. Whole Foods Market attributes the rise to broadening palates, interest in digestive wellness, and the sober-curious movement. Many consumers are also cutting back on sugar, which leaves room for flavors that deliver complexity without added sweetness.


For CPG brands, this opens the door to more adventurous flavor profiles across everyday food categories. Citrus peel can add a bright, bitter edge to salad dressings and marinades, while bitter greens like radicchio and endive bring complexity to prepared salads. In dips and spreads, ingredients like tahini and charred vegetables create deeper, more savory flavors.


Packaged snacks can also tap into the trend with roasted chickpeas, seed-based crackers, and other savory options that balance bitter notes with familiar flavors.


## Bring Your 2027 Product Ideas to Life


Trends move fast, and the brands that win are the ones ready to act on them. At The Fresh Factory, we partner with better-for-you companies to turn emerging ideas into retail-ready products.


Our[in-house R&D team](https://thefreshfactory.co/food-development/) works alongside founders to develop and refine formulas. That might mean removing synthetic dyes from a legacy SKU, adding fiber or functional ingredients to a new product, or balancing bitter notes in a dressing or sauce. And because we’ve been committed to clean label manufacturing from day one, we understand how to deliver great taste and shelf life without relying on artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives.


Transparency is also at the core of how we operate. We were founded on the belief that consumers deserve to know where their food comes from. Our Non-GMO Project approved facilities, ingredient traceability, and testing protocols help brands back up the clean label claims their customers seek.
